method: Manual whole-file review of both files; pinned Git byte comparison. No Windows ACL API execution.
findings: ScanItem returns same empty vector on GetNamedSecurityInfo failure, null DACL, or no qualifying rows. No per-path diagnostics/completeness flag distinguishes these conditions. Empty published result still counts successful StartScan.
Only ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE_TYPE and ACCESS_DENIED_ACE_TYPE processed; inherited ACEs included only at selected roots. Other object/callback/audit ACE forms skipped; no effective-access calculation.
GetSecurityDescriptorControl result unchecked; default control0can yield inherited-enabled label on failure. Generic masks expanded through file mapping before display classification.

BuildScanList comment says snapshot but returns borrowed pointers into live CItem tree, not copied nodes. Actual per-row shared snapshot created only later in ScanItem when first qualifying ACE found. Modal settled-state lifecycle is required for pointer safety.
MTP subtrees skipped, reserved items excluded, every real type path otherwise considered. Reparse-directory handling follows already built model; no independent filesystem-boundary proof.

Parallel ScanItems uses atomic cursor and configured1..16jthreads, joined before returning; cancellation checked between items, not inside potentially blocking descriptor/SID/regex calls. No per-call deadline.

StartScan clears previous results before settled-state guard; cancelled scan deletes all newly produced rows and returns false. Invalid persisted exclusion regex silently ignored. Headless ScanTree has no cancellation callback or diagnostics.
Results vector holds raw owned row pointers, UI control owns published rows. Worker exceptions are not locally caught; no allocation/regex/API fault injection.
limits: No Windows ACL corpus, null-DACL, API-error, cancellation latency, concurrency or headless export runtime test.
Source review cannot convert empty output to proof of absent permissions.
No foreign production code adopted; native pHash investigation remains deferred.
